newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SOUTH AFRICAN MPS TO RELIVE TOWNSHIP SQUALOR.
newsitem.headline: SOUTH AFRICAN MPS TO RELIVE TOWNSHIP SQUALOR.

text.p: A South African parliamentary committee agreed on Wednesday to hold its next meeting in a black township so members could see that their supporters still lived in squalor three years after the end of apartheid.

The chairwoman of the committee on the environment, Gwen Mahlangu, suggested that members forsake the clean, tidy comfort of parliament and hold their next meeting in the sprawling Khayelitsha slum on the outskirts of Cape Town.
The proposal, agreed upon by a majority of committee members, was made during discussion of who was responsible for rubbish removal in black townships.
Mahlangu said she had visited Khayelitsha last weekend and had lost her appetite because it was so dirty.
"We are removed from a number of things, our focus is removed...For how long are we going to turn a blind eye to things that should be changed?" she asked.

"A lot of people are still living in dirt...If I was to go there today and find people exactly where I left them, three years later, I would feel ashamed, because these are the people who voted for us," Mahlangu said.
"They said 'Go and change things for us'...Some of us have been in Cape Town for a very long time, I'm sure we have forgotten about those places," she said.

Mahlangu is a member of President Nelson Mandela's African National Congress, which won South Africa's first all-race election in April 1994 with 62 percent of the vote, crushing the National Party whose apartheid policies left a legacy of deprivation among black communities.
